{{Short description|Average of two consecutive odd primes}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''interprime''' is the [[Arithmetic mean|average]] of two consecutive [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[prime number|prime]]s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|title=Interprime|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Interprime.html|access-date=2020-08-10|website=mathworld.wolfram.com|language=en}}</ref> For example, 9 is an interprime because it is the average of 7 and 11. The first interprimes are:
:4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 26, 30, 34, 39, 42, 45, 50, 56, 60, 64, 69, 72, 76, 81, 86, 93, 99, ... {{OEIS|id=A024675}}
Interprimes cannot be prime themselves (otherwise the primes would not have been consecutive).<ref name=":0" />

Since there are infinitely many primes, there are also infinitely many interprimes.
